metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Bergen County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Palisade & Bluff Section, High-Rise Luxury & Center Core, Coytesville Section, Abbott Boulevard & West Fort Lee
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 2.48%, with an equalization ratio of 74.2%.
Public education represents 54.8% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 34.2%.
Average residential assessment is $430,360, producing an average annual tax bill of $10,672.93.

neighborhoods.name: Palisade & Bluff Section
neighborhoods.character: Spectacular cliffside mansions, luxury modern estates, and high-end residences overlooking the Hudson River and Manhattan skyline
neighborhoods.description: Elite cliffside enclave perched high above the Hudson River with unobstructed skyline views of Manhattan, adjacent to Palisades Interstate Park.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Top assessed tier where individual luxury home assessments exceed $1.8M and tax bills average $32,000+.

neighborhoods.name: High-Rise Luxury & Center Core
neighborhoods.character: World-famous high-rise residential towers (The Modern, Horizon House, Med South, Century Towers) offering resort amenities
neighborhoods.description: Urban luxury center transformed by the George Washington Bridge redevelopment, featuring high-rise living with direct Manhattan commuter transit.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High ratable density provides enormous municipal property tax levy revenues.

neighborhoods.name: Coytesville Section
neighborhoods.character: Historic northern residential neighborhood with single-family colonials, duplexes, and quiet neighborhood streets near Englewood Cliffs
neighborhoods.description: Historic film pioneer neighborhood with traditional suburban residential character and direct access to Route 9W.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Solid middle-tier residential base with consistent assessment appreciation.

neighborhoods.name: Abbott Boulevard & West Fort Lee
neighborhoods.character: Quiet residential street grid with well-kept single-family homes, two-family side-by-sides, and walkability to local schools
neighborhoods.description: Diverse family neighborhood convenient to Fort Lee Community Center, local Korean and Japanese dining corridors, and elementary schools.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Balanced ratables supporting local education without disproportionate municipal debt burden.

equityAnalysis.summary: Fort Lee Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Fort Lee Borough, homeowners pay an average of $10,672.93 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 10.0% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 74.2%, assessed values average ~74.2% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 54.8% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 34.2%, and Bergen County claims 11.0%.
